chunks: Do not be niggardly, nor extravagant that you may later feel reprehensive and constrained.

key_terms.تَبْسُطْهَا: You extend or spread it out, referring to extravagant spending
key_terms.عُنُقِكَ: Your neck, indicating closeness or restriction
key_terms.كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ: Completely or excessively, indicating full extension
key_terms.مَحْسُورًا: Regretful or constrained, often due to poverty or loss
key_terms.مَغْلُولَةً: Bound or chained, referring to stinginess or hoarding wealth
key_terms.مَلُومًا: Reproached or blamed, a state of regret for one's actions

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of not binding your hand to your neck in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted through the lens of *Wasatiyyah* (moderation), extending beyond mere financial prudence to encompass a balanced spiritual and social life. Scholars highlight that 'chaining the hand to the neck' signifies miserliness that hoards wealth at the expense of self and community, while 'spreading it completely' denotes reckless extravagance that leads to *mahsur* (regretful poverty). This balance is viewed as a practical application of the Prophetic tradition of avoiding extremes in all worldly affairs.
